title: Take an empty cup out of a person's trembling hand and put it on the tray, without catching their fingers or pushing their hand
keywords: taking a cup from a person
instruction: Take the cup the person is holding out to you and put it on the coaster on the tray.
context: People with a hand tremor (essential tremor, Parkinson's) hand their cup back after a drink many times a day, at home and in care homes, and whoever takes it takes it from a shaking hand that keeps hold of it. The cup sways about a centimetre each way four or five times a second (4.5 Hz here), the person's fingers wrap its lower half and their little finger carries its weight, and they let go only once they feel that weight taken. So it is caught by the band above their fingers, where a gripper's finger plates have about a centimetre to spare above the palm and fingers, lifted a little until they let go, then lifted clear. Close too low and you catch a finger; push or drag the hand and you hurt them. The shaking is not an event: the hand trembles from the first frame to the last, as a tremor does.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table top (the bed's overbed table). Armrest: firm foam block, vinyl covered, 30 x 16 x 10.8 cm, taped down, x 45.5 to 75.5, centred y 4.9. Trainer right forearm and hand, life size, printed from the task's STL files (PLA, fingers silicone coated): the forearm (1.2 kg with steel-shot ballast) lies free on the armrest pointing at the robot; at the wrist a pan-tilt bracket with two MG90S micro servos, then the palm and thumb, then the four fingers as one block on a third servo at the knuckles; an Arduino runs the task's tremor sketch. The hand is thumb up, palm against the cup's left (+y) side; the fingers wrap the cup's front and right up to 7.1 cm, the thumb its back, the little finger curls under its base, whose weight rests on a microswitch in that finger. Cup: clear polypropylene tumbler, empty, 7 cm across, 14 cm tall, 70 g, base 10 cm up. Cup centre at (37, 0); wrist at (43.8, 4.9), 13.4 cm up. Tremor: pan +-5.5 deg and roll +-3.8 deg, sine, a quarter cycle apart, at 4.5 Hz, all trial. Tray: hospital meal tray 35 x 26 x 1.5 cm centred (26, -22), 9 cm cork coaster at its centre. Both arms start at the ready pose. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: 0, latched for the trial: the cup tips past 45 deg or drops to the table top off the tray (knocked or dropped); the hand is pushed or pulled (the wrist's pan or roll pointer past +-25 deg on its scale, or the forearm moved over 1.5 cm, lifted over 1 cm or turned over 8 deg from its marks on the armrest); or a finger or the thumb is between a gripper's two finger plates as they close (caught). Otherwise, at the end of the trial: 1.0 once the cup has stood upright (within 10 deg) on the tray with its base centre within 1 cm of the coaster's centre (the whole base on the coaster) and no gripper within 7 cm of its axis for 1 s; 0.5 if upright on the tray otherwise; 0.25 if the cup is out of the hand (5 cm clear of every finger) and held by a gripper; 0 otherwise. The person lets go when the cup's base has been off the little finger for 0.25 s. Real trial: a side camera sees the pointers, the fingers and the plates; ruler checks of the forearm's and the cup's marks.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (1 minute at 20 Hz) per trial
reset_notes: Press the sketch's reset button (fingers close), seat the cup in the hand with its base on the little finger, and the forearm on its armrest marks. Check once per session with a slow-motion phone video against a ruler behind the cup: the rim sways 2 to 3.5 cm peak to peak side to side at 4.5 Hz, and the fingers open 0.25 s after the cup is lifted 3 mm.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The servos are joint drives (MG90S torque, 0.25 N m) whose sine targets are written every physics step, so the tremor is the rig's own and a gripper holding the cup steadies it. The trainer hand is rigid, fingers capsules; the cup is held by the fingers' light grip and the little finger, and the release servo opens the fingers as the microswitch would. The forearm is free on the foam.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (reaches toward the cup twice with the left gripper, never takes it). Demo (catch the cup above the fingers, lift until the person lets go, set it on the coaster): 1.0 in 316 steps. Controls: plates round the cup's middle 0 (finger caught); idle 0.
